title: Permissions smoke harness and regression pipeline for RBAC v2
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Provide a stable, fast-running smoke harness plus full regression pipeline that validates RBAC v2 permission tuples end-to-end across: console UI routes, API/SDK calls, Dedicated/Private routing, and SSO/SAML role mappings. The suite must ensure: (1) permission decisions match the policy matrix (golden fixtures), (2) audit logs emit the correct structured events for allow/deny decisions and role-mapping changes, and (3) SAML/SSO role->permission mappings don\u2019t create privilege escalation holes.

Scope and deliverables:
- Implement a lightweight smoke harness that runs in ~3 minutes against a synthetic tenant and verifies a critical subset of permission invariants (create/delete/route/read/observe) across resources (model, deployment, route, workspace).
- Author a set of golden fixture CSV/YAML files that enumerate permission test cases for role permutations (admin, infra, developer, viewer, support). Golden fixtures live in: github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-fixtures (folder: fixtures/v2).
- Expand CI to include a nightly full regression run that exercises all golden fixtures and emits a delta report showing regressions vs the last known-good golden snapshot. Failure of P0 invariants should block canary deploys.
- Add audit-log assertions: each permission decision in the test must correlate to a structured audit event (actor, action, resource, decision, policy_version, kv_diff). Tests must validate log ingestion into the dev audit store (kinesis-dev -> logs-dev index) and check for presence/format.
- Include SAML/SSO simulated assertions: tests will exercise IdP role statements mapping (saml.Role:infra -> Redwood role infra) to ensure mapping does not grant unexpected permissions. Use the saml simulator in infra/test-idp with two mock IdPs (okta-sim and azure-sim).
- Provide a flaky-test mitigation plan: deterministic ordering, idempotent setup/teardown, tokenized resources, and re-run heuristics with exponential backoff.

Acceptance criteria:
- Smoke harness executes in CI pipeline (job: rbac-smoke) and completes under 5 minutes in 90% of runs.
- Nightly regression produces a regression-report artifact and posts annotated PR to the team Slack #security-tests when new diffs are detected.
- Audit-log assertions pass for 95% of test-cases in the nightly run; failures create an incident ticket.
- SAML mapping fuzz tests find zero privilege escalation cases in the seeded fixture set.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not re-implement policy evaluation logic or modify the runtime policy engine. It is a verification harness only.

Notes and constraints:
- We must avoid using production customer data for test fixtures. All test tenants are synthetic.
- Golden fixtures must be versioned and stored with a checksum manifest to enable delta checks.
- Performance targets align with console-2026.03 SLOs for latency-sensitive permission checks.
